title: Seaking Drills Its Nest Into a Boulder
premise: Male Seaking use their drill-like horns to carve nests inside stream boulders.
audiencePromise: See how Seaking turns a river boulder into a safer nest for its eggs.
openLoop: How can a fish protect eggs inside a river rock?
payoff: Seaking hollows out hard riverbed rocks so its eggs avoid the current.

voice.instructions: Speak like a knowledgeable fan sharing a strange discovery. Keep the pace quick, warm, and clear. Stress drill, boulder, and eggs. Pause briefly before the final question.

scenes.headline: A NEST IN STONE
scenes.narration: Seaking drills its nest inside a boulder.
scenes.caption: IT DRILLS A NEST INTO ROCK

scenes.headline: THE BUILDER IS THE MALE
scenes.narration: The male carves stream boulders with the horn on its head.
scenes.caption: THE MALE CARVES THE BOULDER

scenes.headline: RIVERS CAN TAKE THE EGGS
scenes.narration: A nest matters because stream currents can wash the eggs away.
scenes.caption: CURRENT = DANGER

scenes.headline: ITS HORN SPINS
scenes.narration: The horn spins like a drill, steadily hollowing even harder rocks.
scenes.caption: A HORN THAT DRILLS ROCK

scenes.headline: THE BOULDER BECOMES A SHELTER
scenes.narration: So the eggs sit inside the boulder, protected from the current.
scenes.caption: ROCK BECOMES A NEST
